findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed multiple temperature control for food safety foods held past their seven day date marking period:
1) Mushrooms sauce in the downstairs walk in cooler (dated 4/16)
2) French onion soup in the downstairs walk in cooler (dated 4/15)
3) Creme brulée in the upstairs standing cooler (next to the grill) (dated 4/16)
4) Roasted duck in the ground level walk in cooler (dated 4/16)
5) Mushroom sauce in the ground level walk in cooler (dated 4/14)
CORRECTED- the aforementioned foods will be discarded. Continue educating staff about date marking requirements and holding times. Ensure all TCS foods are marked to be used or DISCARDED within seven days (the day of preparation counts as DAY ONE).
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.

2. Both bottom reach-in coolers have food debris inside shelving and bases of units - clean.
3. Walk-in cooler shelving units have food debris built up on them (protein cooler and upstairs cooler in particular). Power wash the shelving units.
4. Microwave upstairs in the party room area is soiled - wash, rinse, sanitize.
5. Ceiling above prep area (not cook line, other side) has dust. Food prep is being conducted here. Clean the ceiling.

Discussed routine cleaning of food-contact surfaces with PIC. Inspector will follow-up on 10/10/22.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-202.13: (A) Insect control devices used to stun or electrocute flying insects shall be designed to retain insect in device. (B) Devices shall be installed where it is not located over FOOD preparation area and dead insects and fragments cannot impel or fall into exposed FOOD or FOOD-EQUIPMENT. 

Observed the insect control device to be above clean food equipment. Move the shelving unit so it is not under the insect control device. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.112: Dead or trapped birds, insects, rodents, and other pests shall be removed from control devices and the PREMISES at a frequency that prevents their accumulation, decomposition, or the attraction of pests. 

(REPEAT) Observed areas of the basement to have dead cockroaches on sticky pads. Ensure staff or pest control company is actively changing out sticky pads. Look under the dry storage shelving for the sticky pads. Discussed with PIC. Ensure dead pests are removed is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 3/18/22.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation. 

Observed the gasket/seal to be coming away from one of the cold holding drawers in the kitchen. Repair the seal. Discussed with PIC. Repair by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the following non-food contact areas to be in need of cleaning:
1. Hood system is heavily soiled (both sides of prep area in kitchen) with grease. Lights under hood are covered in grease. Meacham is due to come out and should be called.
2. Wall directly in front of the prep line has build-up on food splash.
3. All fryers in need of deep cleaning (dust, grease build-up). Interior needs cleaned as well.
4. Entire prep area of kitchen should be pulled out and cleaned under the equipment. Food debris and grease are on flooring.
5. Ceiling has dust build-up above the reach-in coolers/freezer outside of walk-in cooler in kitchen. Dust build-up on ceiling above dish machine area as well. 

Discussed routine cleaning with PIC. Discussed creating a clean-up schedule at least once a month. The facility (prep line area) needs a deep cleaning.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following areas in need of repair:
1. Caulk all holes within the kitchen walls. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 3/18/22.
2. Caulking is needed at the dish machine area. No caulk present between equipment and wall in certain areas. There is a wood board above the equipment that needs re-painted (seal so smooth and easily cleanable).
3. Mop sink is in need of re-caulking (mold build-up).
4. Hand sink upstairs in the party prep kitchen needs holes caulked above it. 

Discussed re-pairs with PIC. Ensure repairs before next routine inspection.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observed many food handler’s licenses to be expired or expiring. Some employees did not have a food handler’s license. The facility is in need of paperwork overhaul. Ensure all employee’s have a food handler’s license within 30 days of employment. Keep copies in a public health binder. Discussed with business manager.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Observed one CFPM to have allergen training; however, the other two do not. Ensure all CFPM’s have allergen training completed. Keep copies in a public health binder. Discussed with business manager.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

(REPEAT) Observed a food handling employee to improperly wash hands. Faucet was turned off without a barrier. Utilize a barrier such as a paper towel to turn off the faucets. Discussed with PIC. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 12/17/21.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.112: Dead or trapped birds, insects, rodents, and other pests shall be removed from control devices and the PREMISES at a frequency that prevents their accumulation, decomposition, or the attraction of pests. 

Observed two areas of the basement (in a corner and under a shelving unit) to have dead cockroaches. Discussed with several employees. Employees cleaned the areas of dead pests. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris. 

Observed the following areas to not be smooth and easily cleanable:
1. Caulk all the holes within the kitchen walls. 
2. Duct tape on the reach-in cooler door (end of the prep line/grill - across from the reach-in freezer) should be removed. Duct tape is not an approved material.

Discussed with PIC. Ensure repairs before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

(REPEAT) Observed improper hand washing by an employee at the upstairs server area (party room). Employee did not use a barrier to turn off the faucet. Discussed with employee. Utilize a paper towel or some kind of barrier to turn off faucets in order to hinder cross contamination. COS. Improper hand washing was an issue during the last routine inspection on 7/27/21.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

Observed the ice basin to have bottles chilling in the ice at the bar in the party room. Cease practice. Ice is utilized in the drinks. This is cross contamination of a food (ice). Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed soda nozzle holder at the main bar to have accumulation of mold and debris. Discussed routine cleaning with employee. Employee washed, rinsed, and sanitized the soda nozzle holder on the request of the Inspector. COS.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.14: FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including (A)-(I) any activities that may have contaminated the hands.  

Observed food handler to walk in to the kitchen with cell phone in hand, begin food prep, don gloves and no hand washing occurred. Discussed with employee. Employee stated she washed hands upstairs. Employees should wash hands when entering kitchen and engaging in food prep, especially after cell phone usage. Discussed with employee. Employee washed hands and then donned gloves. COS.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. 

(REPEAT) Observed salmon to be thawing while still fully wrapped in reduced oxygen packaging (ROP). ROP on product states that fish should be removed from packaging before thawing. Cease practice. Discussed with PIC. Salmon and any other fish/food item with ROP packaging will be removed from the packaging, placed in shallow metal pans, wrapped in Saran Wrap, and date marked. COS. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 6/3/20.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. 

Observed multiple adult cockroaches to be dead behind equipment throughout the basement. Discussed in depth the pest control situation with PIC and employees. Sentinel comes 2x monthly and came the day of the inspection. Traps were located in many places throughout the facility. Facility is actively aware of the pest control issues and maintaining service. See that areas of the basement and beneath the prep tables in the kitchen are routinely washed, rinsed, sanitized and cleaned. Inspector did not see pests under the prep tables. Inspector will follow-up on 8/5/21.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

(REPEAT) Observed large accumulation of frost around the walk-in freezer door in the basement. Discussed routine cleaning with PIC in order to hinder frost accumulation. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 6/3/20 and 12/30/19.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

Observed the shelf under the microwave in the kitchen (nearest the reach-in freezer) to have an accumulation of dust. The light shield by the prep utensils shelves (near utility sink in the kitchen) to have accumulation of dust. Discussed routine cleaning of NonFOOD-contact surfaces with PIC.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment: Three live roaches were observed moving around in the southern section of the prep area. Two were observed on the floor and moved under a cooler when light was directed at them. The last was observed crawling into the side vent of one of the prep coolers. None were observed in food or on food contact surfaces. An inspector will spot check in a couple weeks.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: Many locations throughout the facility are observed with significant accumulation of food debris. This could be a contributing factor and should be addressed. Spot check will check on the progress. Areas included (but not limited to) are under the prep cooler, prep tables, stand up coolers and grill areas.
